edits.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: difficult synthetic food-inventory test photo.
Input image: edit target. Radically rework this staged refrigerator into a believable overstuffed family fridge after a busy week. Keep an ordinary domestic refrigerator, but change the food, arrangement, camera angle, and lighting as needed.
Primary request: an unplanned phone snapshot someone texts while deciding what to cook. Make the entire scene substantially messier and harder to inventory. Portrait composition from slightly above, camera tilted a few degrees, fridge edges cut off naturally.
Scene: Pack the shelves two or three layers deep with roughly twenty to thirty mixed grocery packages and containers. Use uneven stacks of mismatched takeaway boxes and reused tubs, foil-wrapped leftovers, a crumpled half-open cheese bag draped over a container, bags of produce pushed behind cartons, an egg carton wedged under something, a partly used dairy jug near the back, jars and sauces with labels turned sideways, partial packages of deli food, and produce partly hidden in a fogged crisper drawer. Show small gaps into the rear but leave many contents impossible to see. Integrate everything with plausible weight, contact, shelf placement, and overlapping edges.
Remove the artificial big MILK and SPINACH labels entirely. Packaging should look like everyday retail packaging with naturally busy small printing, mostly rotated away, folded, obstructed or unreadable. Nothing should look like neatly separated flash cards for ingredient recognition.
Texture and capture: cloudy plastic, creased bags, condensation, a little dried residue on shelf edges, scratched drawer fronts, mixed warm fridge light and cooler room light, mild real smartphone sensor grain and uneven exposure. The fridge should look lived-in, not abandoned or filthy. No mold spectacle. A few food shapes remain recognizable through the clutter, but item identity, counts, amounts, and expiry cannot be comprehensively resolved.
Avoid: symmetric arrangement, spacious shelves, frontal readable product labels, empty immaculate drawers, studio lighting, food styling, dramatic portrait bokeh, annotations, watermarks, humans. Do not merely put a few extra objects into the original orderly layout; genuinely recompose the packed shelves.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: difficult synthetic food-inventory test photo.
Input image: edit target. Transform it into a substantially more challenging, realistic hurried smartphone capture of a crowded domestic fridge.
Primary request: someone opens the door only halfway at night and snaps a badly framed portrait photo from the side. The near door shelf and its tall condiment bottles obstruct roughly a quarter of the view. Crop parts of both the fridge and the foreground packaging out of frame. Viewpoint slightly tilted and too close, with several overlapping depth planes. It should look like an imperfect usable evidence photo, not an aesthetically composed photograph.
Scene: replace the exposed individual grocery display with dense, casually shoved-in clutter. Include a jumble of partly used crinkled grocery bags and plastic film catching glare; mismatched lidded leftovers stacked at angles; squeezed condiment bottles and jars; a dairy-style carton with its front hidden; a nearly buried closed egg carton; indistinct leafy produce; a cut vegetable wrapped in plastic; and a few other ordinary obscured packages. Many objects are only visible as slivers and some visible patches may belong to one container, not separate objects. Food in a lower drawer is seen through scratched cloudy plastic. The foreground door rack hides some of the shelf behind it.
Capture: harsh small fridge bulb creates a blown highlight on glossy film and strong shadows behind food. The kitchen outside is dark. Add credible low-light phone noise and slight hand-motion softness, while keeping several foreground shapes recognizable. Real smudges, scuffed plastic, an old small spill mark. Packaging print is turned away, tiny, folded or blurred, not blank educational labels. Natural clutter and imperfection, no deliberately grotesque filth or visible mold.
Constraints: no orderly rows, no pristine empty space, no product-style lighting, no isolated specimen ingredients, no readable expiration dates, no explanatory overlays, no watermark, no person. Do not make an entirely unreadable black blur; the important difficulty is occlusion and uncertainty, with limited recognizable food evidence.
